pr_title: REGR: fix consolidation/cache issue with take operation
pr_comments: The non-copying alternative would be to not call `self._consolidate_inplace` in `BlockManager.take`
LGTM; can look into the no-copy solution longer-term

The line `position[position["startdate"] == 0]` goes through `position.take`, which calls `self._mgr.take`, which calls `_consolidate_inplace`, which fails to invalidate the `_item_cache`.

One fix is to restore the `self._consolidate_inplace` done in `NDFrame.take` that was removed in #34389.  Another (my preferred long-term solution) is to remove the `self._consolidate_inplace` done in `BlockManager.take`.

review_comments: i would put in pandas/tests/frame/test_indexing.py (or similar) rather than here.

It's not really an indexing bug, but rather a bug in `take` in combination with indexing before and afterwards (and it's the assign operation that only makes the bug visible), and is specific to the consolidation state of the original dataframe. So it's more a bug in the internal machinery of consolidation / cache.
